groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
W: Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure. Today, we go on a different kind of adventure: Jackson's life of parenting his offspring. David, as a parent of an 11- and a 14-year-old, what is the most interesting issue you are dealing with right now?
M: It's easy to focus on the challenges, but so far, I find these ages to be kind of wonderful. They are independent, and they have their own curiosities and obsessions. You can talk to them about fairly sophisticated subject matter such as politics.
W: Yes, that does sound refreshing compared with talking to younger children. Do they ask you to proofread their essays?
M: Certainly, with writing they do. I really just try to be encouraging. I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement.
W: Are there books that you think are important that your children read, and that all children read?
M: My general thought is to read widely and to incorporate a love for reading. Learning to love to read, I think, is the optimal thing, because it gives you a skill you can take anywhere.
W: So you're not too concerned like some parents with the content they're reading? I know I have some worries about that.
M: Yeah, read what you like. If a child loves graphic novels or comic books, whatever it is, that is turning them on to read and turning on their imagination.
W: I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence. I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager. What do you think?
M: I think it's especially important as they get older to read subject matter that'll open their eyes to the world and people. So I think both fiction and non-fiction are really important because they give you the power to begin to perceive the world through the lives of others.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
M: In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur. Molly, tell us about your business.
W: Well, I sell specialty clothes through a website, mainly for women who have trouble finding suitable clothes in main street shops because of their height or weight. But I do some men's clothes too.
M: How did you get started in this business at such a young age? Are you studying fashion design?
W: Actually, I'm majoring in finance, but I've always loved clothes. And I started making my own at 14.
M: Did you have any sort of training in design or sewing? Or was it a natural ability?
W: I'd have to say no to both. No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters.
M: Why did you persevere? I think most people would give up if they kept failing, especially at that age.
W: I kept on out of necessity. As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops. So I kept trying and developed my skills over time.
M: Well, my notes say you earned $50,000 in profits last year, an extraordinary amount for a 20-year-old student. How did that happen? Did you see a gap in the market and decide to fill it?
W: No. When I started university, some classmates complimented my clothes. And when I said I made them myself, other tall women started asking if I would make theirs. And I did. And before I knew it, I was an entrepreneur.
M: So what are your plans for the future? Do you intend to open a physical store?
W: No. I'll keep things online to keep costs down. But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants. And I hope to add to my range of designs for men.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Researchers have identified a potent new antibiotic compound using artificial intelligence. The antibiotic can kill very dangerous bacteria. According to a study published in the journal Cell, the compound successfully removed deadly strains of bacteria in mice which are resistant to all known antibiotics.
The researchers say this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule. Why does this matter? The answer is antibiotic resistance. This happens when bacteria develop the ability to survive the medications designed to kill them. Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health and the problem is growing. This makes finding new antibiotics very important. However, in recent decades, very few have been developed, and those that have tend to be very similar to drugs already available. The searches also tend to only focus on a narrow spectrum of chemical compounds, but this is where artificial intelligence comes in. Why? To find new drugs, scientists screen molecules to predict how effective they might be. Typically, such screening is done by humans in the lab, which is both costly and slow. Artificial intelligence is different. It's fast, and it can process a high volume. It can screen hundreds of millions of compounds to identify a few interesting candidates that require experimental testing. Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic. Some experts assert that this work signifies a paradigm shift in antibiotic discovery. It could change drug discovery more generally.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
A recent study overturned what we think we know about lying. Most of us have a theory about how to tell if someone is telling a lie. We may develop that theory from observations of those people we know well and see regularly, but we tend to generalize what we gather from that unscientific daily research and make it a universal theory.
So we might imagine that liars have evasive eyes, or the opposite—they simply stare at you. Or perhaps it is more generally nervous behavior we associate with lies. Whatever the particular theory, it's usually based on close observation of people we know. And we get lots of practice. On average, we're lied to some 200 times per day. These are mostly harmless lies, but lies nonetheless.
But there's a problem with our theories, even though they're based on all these observations. The average person—you and me—tested rigorously on how well we detect lies fails to do better than chance. That's well established over many studies and lots of attempts by researchers to work out reliable ways to detect lies. It's even relatively easy to fool lie detectors, the gold standard of lie detection, by training yourself in breathing techniques and symptom suppression.
Is there any way to get better at detecting lies? The new research offers some surprising advice. Stop looking and listen instead. It turns out that if we're unable to see the face, but rather focus on the voice of the person in question, our accuracy rate improves considerably.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful and undemanding; show great pleasure when a doctor comes into your room, even if the visit is brief and useless. Don't challenge anyone with authority unless you are famous or very rich.
Those are a few strategies for dealing with today's American medical establishment. What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration. But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that. In his book, A Whole New Life, novelist Reynolds Price recalls that his doctors chose a crowded hallway as the place to tell him he might have a tumor on his spinal cord. It did not occur to the two physicians that a hallway was not the most appropriate place for that particular piece of news.
My surgeon, who is in his mid-thirties, looks tired. He has been overwhelmed with patients who have fallen on the winter ice. He is a witty man, but sometimes his wit is unwelcome.
"The health insurance company Blue Cross wants me to put you out in the snow tomorrow afternoon," he tells me after I have been in the hospital for more than a week. I'm terrified because I have no idea where to go. I cannot walk or even lift my leg a few inches. The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot. But my complaints about her only annoy my surgeon. "I have to work with these people," he tells my friend, Dr. Karen Brudney, when she mercifully intervenes on my behalf and arranges for me to be transferred to another hospital.
"If you say one negative thing, they get defensive," she tells me later. "They have this kind of institutional loyalty. Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse. When people know you have their names, they behave better. And," Brudney adds, "if you, as a patient, suggest that you might like to control even part of the situation or be consulted or informed, then you are considered difficult. They want you to be totally passive. The entire health care system, particularly hospitals and nursing homes, exists for reasons that have nothing to do with taking care of patients. Patients are incidental."

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
There are probably teams you've worked with but you never want to work with again. But there must have also been other teams that you would prize reuniting with professionally. In other words, your team had vitality. Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up.
What characteristics of a team make its members more likely to stay in contact despite no longer working together? This question has been answered recently in a study published in a business journal.
One of the two key factors the research team discovered is sameness. Specifically, sharing the same gender or ethnic origin. The more members of a team share similar demographics, the more inclined they will be to remain associates long after the team has served its purpose. After ties are established, similarity strengthens them. As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration. In effect, people tend to create stronger and longer-lasting connections with similar others. Someone who looks and sounds different from us may have the resources we need to be more successful. Yet, we find them to be significantly less credible simply because they are different. If you are a fierce advocate of workplace diversity, you'll no doubt be horrified by such a revelation.
The second factor identified by the researchers is the quality of the relationships among the team members. The more they trust one another, share the same goals and depend on each other for the achievement of those goals, the stronger their chances of maintaining their connections, despite no longer working as one team. Teams with quality relationships have a shared belief that it's safe to take risks with each other, and their members are obliged to share the workload and help out.
From personal experience, I can see both the truth and the inconsistency of such studies. The truth is some of my closest friendships were formed as a result of having worked together on teams, and I actively seek opportunities to work with them again. The inconsistency, though, is that I've never worked for a team more successful and cohesive than the one of which I am a member right now. And yet, the four of us have very little in common and are completely different demographically. So I am unlikely to question the value of a diverse workforce.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
An American researcher who studied 600 millionaires found how rich you can get comes down to six wealth factors. She found that six behaviors are related to net worth potential, regardless of age or income. These were thriftiness, confidence, responsibility, planning, focus and social indifference.
Being thrifty comes as no great surprise. Spending above your means, spending instead of saving for retirement, spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy, makes you a slave to the paycheck. "Even with an astronomical level of income," she wrote, "to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%."
Having confidence is another key characteristic, as it helps people to be thrifty. It takes confidence to live within your means. It also takes confidence to invest properly. Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investments alone and focus on a long-term investment plan. But people can't invest or manage their own money without accepting responsibility for the outcomes. Many millionaires take on personal responsibility, and most also happen to be self-made, meaning they didn't acquire their wealth through luck. Millionaires don't count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don't blame anyone else if they fall short. They focus on things they can control and align their daily habits to the goals they have set for themselves. They tend to be goal-oriented and hard workers, which enables them to plan financially and focus on seeing those plans through. 92% of the millionaires surveyed developed a long term plan for their money and 97% almost always achieved the goals they set for themselves.
And it is these behaviors that make it easy for them to be socially indifferent. They resist lifestyle creep, the tendency to spend more whenever one earns more. Essentially, they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others or what they have acquired. Instead of being focused on what might make them happy today, they're focused on their long-term wealth-building plan.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about David Jackson from the conversation?
options: He is a staff writer.
He is an adventurer.
He is an author of fiction.
He is a father of four kids.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about David Jackson from the conversation? 

 【翻译】 从对话中我们了解到关于David Jackson的什么信息? 
 A)  他是一名专职撰稿人。 
 B)  他是一名冒险家。 
 C)  他是一名小说作家。 
 D)  他是四个孩子的父亲。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） He is a staff writer. 
 【定位】 P1 Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure. 
 David Jackson 先生，《纽约客》的专职撰稿人，以其纪实类冒险题材的书而闻名。 

 【信号】 开场介绍句直接报身份 。主持人开场第一句就用同位语把人物头衔报全：a staff writer at the New Yorker。人物介绍题的答案信号就是这种"姓名 + 同位语头衔"的引入句，听到立刻锁定。 

 【替换】 a staff writer at the New Yorker ↔ He is a staff writer. 原句同位语→选项主系表，几乎原词对应 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 原文说他 is known for his non-fiction books of adventure——写冒险题材的书，是"写冒险的人"不是"亲历冒险的人"。He is an adventurer. 盗用 adventure 一词，把"写冒险书"偷换成"他本人是冒险家"，听到 adventure 就选会中招。  借用原文：is known for his non-fiction books of adventure 

 C) 与原文相反 原文明确是 non-fiction books（纪实/非虚构），He is an author of fiction. 却说他写 fiction（虚构小说），正好把 non-fiction 的 non 抹掉、极性反了。听到 fiction 这半个原词就选，等于没听清前面的否定前缀。  借用原文：non-fiction books of adventure 

 D) 未提及 原文只说他有 an 11- and a 14-year-old（一个 11 岁、一个 14 岁，共两个孩子），He is a father of four kids. 凭空说"四个孩子"。four 这个数字原文从未出现，是偷改数字的陷阱。

questions.prompt: What does the man think of young teenagers?
options: They are interested in fairy tales.
They are curious and autonomous.
They are a headache to their parents.
They are ignorant of politics.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man think of young teenagers? 

 【翻译】 男士对年轻青少年有什么看法? 
 A)  他们对童话故事感兴趣。 
 B)  他们好奇且自主。 
 C)  他们让父母头疼。 
 D)  他们对政治一无所知。 

 【答案】 B （态度观点题） They are curious and autonomous. 
 【定位】 P2 They are independent, and they have their own curiosities and obsessions. 
 他们很独立，有自己的好奇心和着迷的东西。 

 【信号】 被问者的正面评价应答 。女方问他这阶段孩子的情况，男方应答先说 I find these ages to be kind of wonderful，再具体说 They are independent, and they have their own curiosities。对话题答案落在被问者的应答里，wonderful 与 independent、curiosities 是定调的正面信号。 

 【替换】 They are independent ↔ They are curious and autonomous. independent=autonomous 同义替换 
 their own curiosities ↔ curious 名词 curiosities→形容词 curious 词形转换 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 原文说能和孩子聊 sophisticated subject matter such as politics，即谈"成熟话题如政治"，反衬他们不幼稚；They are interested in fairy tales. 童话与原文要表达的"能聊成熟话题"恰恰相反，且 fairy tales 原文根本没提，是借"孩子"语境硬造的话题。  借用原文：sophisticated subject matter such as politics 

 C) 与原文相反 男方明明说 I find these ages to be kind of wonderful（觉得这年纪很好），They are a headache to their parents. 却说孩子让父母头疼，与他的正面评价完全相反。这是把褒义答案反向设成贬义的陷阱。  借用原文：I find these ages to be kind of wonderful 

 D) 原词陷阱 原文说能和孩子聊 politics，恰恰说明他们"懂/能聊政治"；They are ignorant of politics. 盗用 politics 原词，却说他们"对政治无知"，意思正好反过来。听到 politics 就选会直接掉坑。  借用原文：such as politics
questions.spoken_text: What does the man think of young teenagers?

questions.prompt: How does the man help his kids with their essays?
options: He offers them ample editorial guidance.
He recommends model essays to them.
He gives them encouragement.
He teaches them proofreading.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How does the man help his kids with their essays? 

 【翻译】 男士如何帮助他的孩子们写作文? 
 A)  他为他们提供充分的编辑指导。 
 B)  他向他们推荐范文。 
 C)  他给予他们鼓励。 
 D)  他教他们校对。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） He gives them encouragement. 
 【定位】 P4 I really just try to be encouraging. I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement. 
 我真的只是尽量给予鼓励。我觉得在这个年纪，编辑式的指导不如鼓励来得重要。 

 【信号】 取舍句 less important than 落在后半 。男方先表态 I really just try to be encouraging，再用取舍句 editorial guidance is less important than encouragement。"A is less important than B" 的信号是：被贬低的 A（指导）是陪衬，强调的 B（鼓励）才是答案。 

 【替换】 I really just try to be encouraging ↔ He gives them encouragement. be encouraging→give encouragement 形容词转名词 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 He offers them ample editorial guidance. 盗用原文 editorial guidance 原词，可原文恰恰说它 less important than encouragement——他不强调指导。听到 editorial guidance 就选，正好掉进"被贬低项"的坑，且 ample（大量）更与他"只是尽量鼓励"的克制相反。  借用原文：editorial guidance is less important than encouragement 

 B) 未提及 He recommends model essays to them. 借了 essays 这个语境词（女方确实问到 proofread their essays），但"推荐范文（model essays）"这件事男方从没说过，是凭"帮写作"语境硬造的做法。 
 D) 张冠李戴 proofread 这个词确实出现，但它出自女方提问 Do they ask you to proofread their essays?，是"孩子请他校对"，并非"他教孩子校对"。He teaches them proofreading. 把女方问句里的词搬来、又改成"他教校对"，既盗原词又错了施动方。  借用原文：Do they ask you to proofread their essays?
questions.spoken_text: How does the man help his kids with their essays?

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about herself when she was a teenager?
options: Her tastes in books changed.
She realized the power of reading.
Her reading opened her eyes to the world.
She began to perceive the world differently.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about herself when she was a teenager? 

 【翻译】 女士说她十几岁时是什么情况? 
 A)  她对书籍的品味发生了变化。 
 B)  她意识到了阅读的力量。 
 C)  她的阅读让她开阔了眼界。 
 D)  她开始以不同的方式感知世界。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Her tastes in books changed. 
 【定位】 P9 I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence. I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager. 
 我觉得孩子的读书口味会随着进入青春期而改变。我知道我自己当年读中学时口味确实变了。 

 【信号】 mine + when I was a teenager 锁定她谈自己 。女方说 I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager，mine 回指 tastes in books，when I was a teenager 正对题干限定。第一人称 mine/I 加"少年时"，是"她说自己"的答案信号。 

 【替换】 children's tastes in books change ↔ Her tastes in books changed. mine did 还原为 her tastes changed 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 She realized the power of reading. 里的 power 出自男方 they give you the power to begin to perceive the world，是男方谈读书的话，不是女方说自己；且女方从没说她"意识到读书的力量"。既错主语又属未提及。  借用原文：they give you the power to begin to perceive the world 

 C) 张冠李戴 Her reading opened her eyes to the world. 盗用男方 read subject matter that'll open their eyes to the world 的原词 open eyes to the world，但这是男方对"孩子该读什么"的看法，主语既不是"她"、内容也非她自述。听到 open eyes 就选会被男方的话误导。  借用原文：open their eyes to the world 

 D) 原词陷阱 She began to perceive the world differently. 盗用男方 to perceive the world through the lives of others 的 perceive the world，但这同样是男方对读书意义的论述，非女方谈自己。与 C 是一对孪生干扰，靠"主语是谁"才能切开。  借用原文：perceive the world through the lives of others

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the woman?
options: She is a website designer.
She is a university graduate.
She is a main street store owner.
She is a successful entrepreneur.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the woman? 

 【翻译】 关于这位女士我们了解到什么? 
 A)  她是一名网站设计师。 
 B)  她是一名大学毕业生。 
 C)  她是一家实体店的店主。 
 D)  她是一位成功的企业家。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） She is a successful entrepreneur. 
 【定位】 P1 In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur. 
 在本期《财富对话》中，我们的嘉宾是莫莉·桑德斯，一名大学生，也是一位成功的年轻创业者。 

 【信号】 主持人开场介绍嘉宾的同位语 。答案信号是开场白里介绍嘉宾身份的同位语 a university student and a successful young entrepreneur——访谈类听力里，嘉宾身份几乎都在主持人开场这句 our guest is… 后面交代。 

 【替换】 a successful young entrepreneur ↔ She is a successful entrepreneur. 近乎同词，只省去 young 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音确实说她是 a university student，She is a university graduate. 借此设套；但一来题问我们了解到什么，主持人重点捧的是 successful entrepreneur，二来 student（在读）不等于 graduate（已毕业），身份还被偷改了。  借用原文：a university student 

 A) 过度推断 后文她说 I sell specialty clothes through a website，但用网站卖衣服不等于她是做网站的设计师，She is a website designer. 是从 website 一词过度联想出来的。  借用原文：I sell specialty clothes through a website 

 C) 与原文相反 她明确说将来 I'll keep things online to keep costs down，根本不开实体店，She is a main street store owner. 与原文相反；main street 还是她顾客买不到衣服的地方，并非她开店之处。  借用原文：I'll keep things online to keep costs down

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about the clothes she made at first?
options: They were repeatedly rejected by shops.
They were popular with her classmates.
They showed her natural talent.
They were mostly failures.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about the clothes she made at first? 

 【翻译】 关于她最初制作的衣服,这位女士说了什么? 
 A)  它们被商店反复拒绝。 
 B)  它们在她的同学中很受欢迎。 
 C)  它们展现了她的天赋。 
 D)  它们大多是失败之作。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They were mostly failures. 
 【定位】 P6 No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters. 
 没人教过我做衣服，而且我最初做的大多数东西都是惨不忍睹的失败品。 

 【信号】 被问者直接应答里的自我评价词 。主持人问她是否有天赋，她应答中的 most of the things I made at first were disasters 是直接评价句，disasters 这个强贬义词就是答案信号。 

 【替换】 were disasters ↔ They were mostly failures. disasters 约等于 failures 的同义替换 

 【排除】 C) 原词陷阱 主持人问 Or was it a natural ability?，They showed her natural talent. 盗用了 natural 一词；但她明确回答 I'd have to say no to both（天赋、培训都没有），所以显出天赋恰与原文相反。  借用原文：Or was it a natural ability? 

 A) 未提及 They were repeatedly rejected by shops. 听着像创业故事，但录音从没说她最初的衣服被商店反复拒收；她说的是顾客在 main street shops 买不到合身的，张冠李戴了。 
 B) 张冠李戴 同学称赞她衣服确有其事——some classmates complimented my clothes，They were popular with her classmates. 借此设套；但那是她上大学后的事，不是最初（14岁）做的，时间错位。  借用原文：some classmates complimented my clothes

questions.prompt: Why did the woman persevere in making clothes for herself?
options: She had a strong interest in doing it.
She did not like ready-made clothes.
She could not find clothes of her size.
She found clothes in shops unaffordable.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why did the woman persevere in making clothes for herself? 

 【翻译】 这位女士为什么坚持为自己制作衣服? 
 A)  她对做这件事有浓厚的兴趣。 
 B)  她不喜欢成衣。 
 C)  她找不到适合自己尺码的衣服。 
 D)  她觉得商店里的衣服买不起。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） She could not find clothes of her size. 
 【定位】 P8 I kept on out of necessity. As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops. 
 我是出于无奈才坚持下来的。如你所见，我个子很高，在普通商店里找不到合身的衣服。 

 【信号】 原因短语 out of necessity 引出理由 。答案信号是因果短语 out of necessity（出于必需），其后紧跟的 I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me 就是真正原因。 

 【替换】 I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops ↔ She could not find clothes of her size. fit me 约等于 of her size 的同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 她确说过 I've always loved clothes，She had a strong interest in doing it. 借喜爱设套；但那解释的是她为何开始做衣服，题问的是为何坚持，她坚持的理由是无奈，不是兴趣。  借用原文：I've always loved clothes 

 D) 未提及 She found clothes in shops unaffordable. 与C都涉及商店的衣服，迷惑性强；但录音说的是找不到合身的，从未提到买不起、太贵，价格问题纯属杜撰。 
 B) 未提及 She did not like ready-made clothes. 听着合理，但录音只说商店里没有合她身的，从没说她不喜欢现成衣服；她做衣服是因买不到，不是因厌恶成衣。
questions.spoken_text: Why did the woman persevere in making clothes for herself?

questions.prompt: What does the woman plan to do in the future?
options: Study fashion design at college.
Improve her marketing strategy.
Add designs for women.
Expand her business.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman plan to do in the future? 

 【翻译】 这位女士将来打算做什么? 
 A)  在大学学习时装设计。 
 B)  改进她的营销策略。 
 C)  增加女装设计。 
 D)  扩大她的业务。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Expand her business. 
 【定位】 P12 But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants. And I hope to add to my range of designs for men. 
 不过我会增加儿童服装，男孩女孩都做，可能还会做婴幼儿的。我也希望扩充我给男士设计的产品线。 

 【信号】 将来意图信号 I will 与 I hope to 。答案信号是 I will add more clothes for children 与 I hope to add to my range of designs for men 里的 will、hope to——它们标志将来计划，后接的增加品类即答案。 

 【替换】 add more clothes for children ↔ Expand her business. 具体加品类等于概括的扩展生意 

 【排除】 C) 偷换概念 她确说 add to my range of designs for men，Add designs for women. 却把对象由 men（男士）偷换成 women（女士），方向都改错了，且她加的远不止男装。  借用原文：add to my range of designs for men 

 A) 原词陷阱 前文主持人问 Are you studying fashion design?，Study fashion design at college. 盗用了 fashion design；但她回答 I'm majoring in finance，学的是金融，更没把学时装设计当未来计划。  借用原文：Are you studying fashion design? 

 B) 未提及 Improve her marketing strategy. 听着像生意人会做的事，但录音谈未来时只说加品类、保持线上控成本，从没提改进营销策略。
questions.spoken_text: What does the woman plan to do in the future?

questions.prompt: What have researchers done for the first time in history?
options: Utilizing artificial intelligence to find a powerful new antibiotic.
Discovering bacteria which are resistant to all known antibiotics.
Identifying bacterial strains that are most harmful to human health.
Removing a deadly strain of bacteria in humans with a new antibiotic.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What have researchers done for the first time in history? 

 【翻译】 研究人员首次在历史上做了什么? 
 A)  利用人工智能找到一种强效的新型抗生素。 
 B)  发现对所有已知抗生素都具有耐药性的细菌。 
 C)  识别出对人类健康危害最大的细菌菌株。 
 D)  用一种新型抗生素清除人体内的致命细菌菌株。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Utilizing artificial intelligence to find a powerful new antibiotic. 
 【定位】 P2 The researchers say this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule. 
 研究者表示，这是首次有人用人工智能来发现一种强效的新型抗生素分子。 

 【信号】 first time 与题干同标志 。录音里 this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule 出现了与题干 for the first time 完全对应的标志短语 the first time，听到这个标志就锁定这句是答案句。 

 【替换】 artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule ↔ Utilizing artificial intelligence to find a powerful new antibiotic 被动转主动/同义改写 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 项 Discovering bacteria which are resistant to all known antibiotics 盗用了录音第一段 resistant to all known antibiotics 这串原词，但录音说的是新抗生素清除了这些耐药菌、不是去发现耐药菌，听到熟悉的 resistant 就选会落入陷阱。  借用原文：resistant to all known antibiotics 

 C) 未提及 C 项 Identifying bacterial strains that are most harmful to human health 说识别最有害的菌株，录音通篇没说研究者去给菌株按危害排序或识别哪种最有害，属未提及。 
 D) 原词陷阱 D 项 Removing a deadly strain of bacteria in humans with a new antibiotic 盗用了第一段 removed deadly strains of bacteria 的原词，但录音说清除发生在 in mice（小鼠）身上、不是 in humans，且本题问的首次成就是用 AI 找药、不是清除细菌，原词对、主体与考点都错。  借用原文：removed deadly strains of bacteria in mice
questions.spoken_text: What have researchers done for the first time in history?

questions.prompt: What makes it important to find new antibiotic drugs?
options: Ever-increasing strains of bacteria.
Bacteria's resistance to antibiotics.
The similarity between known drugs.
The growing threat of bacteria to health.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What makes it important to find new antibiotic drugs? 

 【翻译】 是什么使得寻找新的抗生素药物变得重要? 
 A)  不断增加的细菌菌株。 
 B)  细菌对抗生素的耐药性。 
 C)  已知药物之间的相似性。 
 D)  细菌对健康日益增长的威胁。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Bacteria's resistance to antibiotics. 
 【定位】 P2 Why does this matter? The answer is antibiotic resistance. This happens when bacteria develop the ability to survive the medications designed to kill them. 
 这为什么重要？答案是抗生素耐药性。当细菌发展出在那些本该杀死它们的药物下存活的能力时，耐药性就出现了。 

 【信号】 自问自答的因果信号 。录音用一个自设问 Why does this matter? 紧跟一句直答 The answer is antibiotic resistance，这种自问自答正是篇章独白明示原因的强信号，答案就藏在 The answer is 之后。 

 【替换】 The answer is antibiotic resistance ↔ Bacteria's resistance to antibiotics 同义短语换序表述 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 项 Ever-increasing strains of bacteria 说细菌菌株不断增多，录音只说耐药性问题在加重（the problem is growing），从未说菌株数量在增加，属未提及。 
 C) 原词陷阱 C 项 The similarity between known drugs 盗用了录音 tend to be very similar to drugs already available 里的 similar，但录音说新药彼此相似是研发不足的表现、不是让找新药变重要的原因，原词对、角色错。  借用原文：tend to be very similar to drugs already available 

 D) 偷换概念 D 项 The growing threat of bacteria to health 盗用了录音 Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health and the problem is growing 里的 threat 与 growing，但录音说的是耐药性对健康是威胁、主语是耐药性，选项却换成 bacteria 对健康的威胁，把本题原因从耐药性偷换成笼统的细菌威胁。  借用原文：Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health and the problem is growing
questions.spoken_text: What makes it important to find new antibiotic drugs?

questions.prompt: What does the passage say artificial intelligence is able to do in antibiotic research?
options: Dispense with experimental testing.
Predict whether compounds are toxic.
Foresee human reaction to antibiotics.
Combat bacteria's resistance to antibiotics.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say artificial intelligence is able to do in antibiotic research? 

 【翻译】 文章说人工智能能够在抗生素研究中做什么? 
 A)  省去实验性测试。 
 B)  预测化合物是否有毒。 
 C)  预见人类对抗生素的反应。 
 D)  对抗细菌对抗生素的耐药性。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Predict whether compounds are toxic. 
 【定位】 P2 Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic. 
 人工智能还能够预测某些化合物是否可能有毒。 

 【信号】 able to 直陈功能 。录音 Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic 里 is also able to 与题干 is able to 直接呼应，是明示 AI 一项能力的功能句，听到 able to 即锁定。 

 【替换】 predict if compounds are likely to be toxic ↔ Predict whether compounds are toxic if 换 whether 的近原词改写 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 项 Dispense with experimental testing 盗用了录音 a few interesting candidates that require experimental testing 里的 experimental testing，但录音说的是 AI 筛出少数候选物仍需做实验测试，恰恰没免去测试，选项却说彻底免去，与原文相反。  借用原文：a few interesting candidates that require experimental testing 

 C) 偷换概念 C 项 Foresee human reaction to antibiotics 盗用了录音 predict 的近义动作，但录音说 AI 预测的是化合物是否有毒，从没说预测人体对抗生素的反应，把预测对象由化合物毒性偷换成人体反应。  借用原文：predict if compounds are likely to be toxic 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 项 Combat bacteria's resistance to antibiotics 盗用了全文反复出现的 antibiotic resistance 这一热词，但本题问的是 AI 本身能做什么（筛分子、预测毒性），AI 并不直接对抗耐药性、对抗耐药性是研发新药的最终目的，原词对、答非所问。  借用原文：Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health
questions.spoken_text: What does the passage say artificial intelligence is able to do in antibiotic research?

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how do most people detect lying?
options: By theorization.
By generalization.
By observation.
By conversation.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 According to the passage, how do most people detect lying? 

 【翻译】 根据文章，大多数人如何识破谎言？ 
 A)  通过理论推导。 
 B)  通过归纳概括。 
 C)  通过观察。 
 D)  通过交谈。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） By observation. 
 【定位】 P1 We may develop that theory from observations of those people we know well and see regularly, but we tend to generalize what we gather from that unscientific daily research and make it a universal theory. 
 我们可能是从对身边熟识、常见之人的观察中形成那套"看人说谎"的理论的，但我们往往会把从这种不科学的日常观察里得来的东西加以归纳，把它当成放之四海皆准的理论。 

 【信号】 起源信号 develop … from 。develop that theory from observations 里的 develop … from 点明"这套判断说谎的理论来自哪里"，正是"靠什么方式"的答案落点；后面虽有 generalize，但那是把观察所得再加工，最初的获取方式仍是 observations。 

 【替换】 from observations of those people we know well ↔ By observation. 复数 observations 概括为 observation 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音反复出现 theory、universal theory，A 项 By theorization.（靠理论化）就是拿这个原词来骗；但录音说理论是"从观察中得来"，获取方式是观察，不是"靠理论化"去判断说谎。  借用原文：make it a universal theory 

 B) 原词陷阱 录音确实说了 we tend to generalize，B 项 By generalization. 就盗这个词；但 generalize 是"把观察所得再归纳推广"的后续动作，不是"多数人最初靠什么发现说谎"——题问的是 detect 的方式，那是观察。  借用原文：we tend to generalize what we gather 

 D) 未提及 By conversation.（靠交谈）与 observation 词形相近，最易听混，但录音通篇没说人们靠"交谈"来识谎，属未提及。
questions.spoken_text: According to the passage, how do most people detect lying?

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about most lies?
options: They are easy to detect.
They are well intended.
They are groundless.
They are harmless.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about most lies? 

 【翻译】 文章关于大多数谎言说了什么？ 
 A)  它们很容易识破。 
 B)  它们是善意的。 
 C)  它们是毫无根据的。 
 D)  它们是无害的。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They are harmless. 
 【定位】 P2 On average, we're lied to some 200 times per day. These are mostly harmless lies, but lies nonetheless. 
 平均而言，我们每天被骗约 200 次。这些大多是无害的谎言，但仍然是谎言。 

 【信号】 直接定性 mostly harmless lies 。These are mostly harmless lies 一句直接给 most lies 下定性词 harmless（无害），是答案句；后面 but lies nonetheless 只是强调它们仍算谎言，不改"无害"这一性质。 

 【替换】 mostly harmless lies ↔ They are harmless. 原词 harmless 几乎直给 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 They are easy to detect. 与录音相反：后文 fails to do better than chance 说人识谎并不强、谎言并不"易察觉"，此项反了。  借用原文：fails to do better than chance 

 B) 未提及 They are well intended.（出于善意）听上去顺理成章，但录音只说谎言"无害"，从没说它们"出于善意"，是未提及。 
 C) 张冠李戴 录音说人们的识谎"理论"有问题（there's a problem with our theories），They are groundless. 像是把"无根据"安到了 lies 头上；但题问的是 most lies，谎言本身并未被说成"无根据"，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：there's a problem with our theories
questions.spoken_text: What does the passage say about most lies?

questions.prompt: What have many studies uncovered about the average person's lie detection?
options: Mostly by chance.
Basically objective.
Subject to their mental alertness.
Dependent on their analytical ability.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What have many studies uncovered about the average person's lie detection? 

 【翻译】 许多研究揭示了普通人识破谎言的什么情况？ 
 A)  主要靠运气。 
 B)  基本客观。 
 C)  取决于他们的精神警觉性。 
 D)  取决于他们的分析能力。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Mostly by chance. 
 【定位】 P3 The average person—you and me—tested rigorously on how well we detect lies fails to do better than chance. 
 普通人——你我这样的人——在被严格测试识谎能力时，表现并不比碰运气更好。 

 【信号】 结论信号 fails to do better than chance 。fails to do better than chance 是这段的研究结论落点：普通人识谎"不比瞎猜强"；下一句 That's well established over many studies 又点明这是多项研究确证的，正对题干 many studies。 

 【替换】 fails to do better than chance ↔ Mostly by chance. "不比碰运气强"="基本靠运气" 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 Basically objective.（基本客观）与录音相反：录音说普通人识谎不比碰运气强，谈不上客观可靠，方向反了。  借用原文：fails to do better than chance 

 C) 未提及 Subject to their mental alertness.（取决于心理警觉）听着像研究会得出的结论，但录音只说"不比碰运气强"，从没说识谎"取决于警觉性"，是未提及。 
 D) 未提及 Dependent on their analytical ability.（取决于分析能力）同样未被录音提及；录音的结论是结果"靠运气"，而非把识谎归因于某种能力。
questions.spoken_text: What have many studies uncovered about the average person's lie detection?

questions.prompt: What advice does the new research offer regarding lie detection?
options: Looking the speaker in the eye.
Listening carefully to the speaker.
Measuring the speaker's breathing rate.
Focusing on the speaker's facial expressions.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What advice does the new research offer regarding lie detection? 

 【翻译】 新研究就识破谎言提出了什么建议？ 
 A)  直视说话者的眼睛。 
 B)  仔细倾听说话者。 
 C)  测量说话者的呼吸频率。 
 D)  关注说话者的面部表情。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Listening carefully to the speaker. 
 【定位】 P4 The new research offers some surprising advice. Stop looking and listen instead. 
 新研究给出了一个出人意料的建议：别再看了，改成去听。 

 【信号】 建议+对比信号 Stop … and … instead 。Stop looking and listen instead 是直白的祈使建议句，且用 Stop looking 与 listen instead 构成"舍看取听"的对比，落点明确在"听"；前句 offers some surprising advice 已预告这就是建议。 

 【替换】 listen instead ↔ Listening carefully to the speaker. listen=Listening to the speaker 
 focus on the voice of the person in question ↔ Listening carefully to the speaker. 关注声音=认真听说话者 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 Looking the speaker in the eye. 属"看"派，而录音建议恰恰是 Stop looking（别看了）；它盗用了"看"这个动作来骗，方向却与建议相反。  借用原文：Stop looking 

 C) 张冠李戴 录音的 breathing 出现在第 3 段——说骗过测谎仪靠 training yourself in breathing techniques，与"新研究的建议"无关；Measuring the speaker's breathing rate. 把这个原词搬来当建议，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：training yourself in breathing techniques 

 D) 与原文相反 录音说 if we're unable to see the face 时准确率反而上升，Focusing on the speaker's facial expressions. 把 face 搬来，方向却相反——建议是别盯脸、去听，看表情正是要放弃的做法。  借用原文：if we're unable to see the face
questions.spoken_text: What advice does the new research offer regarding lie detection?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about most American hospitals?
options: They don't treat patients with due respect.
They witness a lot of doctor-patient conflicts.
They have to deal with social workers' strikes.
They don't care how much patients have to pay.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about most American hospitals? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于大多数美国医院说了什么? 
 A)  它们没有以应有的尊重对待病人。 
 B)  它们目睹了许多医患冲突。 
 C)  它们必须应对社会工作者的罢工。 
 D)  它们不关心病人要支付多少钱。 

 【答案】 A （态度观点题） They don't treat patients with due respect. 
 【定位】 P2 What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration. But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that. 
 病人想要的是被尊重、被体谅地对待。但据我的经验，愿意这样做的医院和医生太少了。 

 【信号】 转折 But + 程度词 too few 。答案落在转折词后：But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that。前半句说『病人想被尊重』是铺垫，But 之后才是主讲人的真实判断——能做到的医院太少，这正是定性句。 

 【替换】 too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that ↔ They don't treat patients with due respect. 肯否定转换：很少做到=不做到 
 treated with respect and consideration ↔ with due respect 同义改写：respect=due respect 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 They witness a lot of doctor-patient conflicts. 借用了全篇的医患话题，听着像在讲医患关系，但原文只说医院少有尊重病人，从没说医院『目睹大量医患冲突』，属于顺着话题硬编。 
 C) 原词陷阱 They have to deal with social workers' strikes. 盗了后文出现的 social worker 一词，制造『听到原词就想选』的诱惑。但原文 The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot 里 strikes 是『让我觉得』之意（strike sb as），与『罢工 strike』完全无关，且这是讲个人遭遇，不是医院的总体特征。  借用原文：The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot 

 D) 未提及 They don't care how much patients have to pay. 把话题引向『收费』，但全篇主讲人谈的是尊重、知情、被动顺从，从未谈医院在不在乎病人花多少钱，费用维度是凭空添加的。
questions.spoken_text: What does the speaker say about most American hospitals?

questions.prompt: What does Karen Brudney suggest patients do?
options: Appear submissive and grateful to doctors and nurses.
Express a strong desire to be consulted or informed.
Refrain from saying anything that sounds negative.
Note down the names of all the doctors and nurses.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does Karen Brudney suggest patients do? 

 【翻译】 Karen Brudney建议病人做什么? 
 A)  在医生和护士面前表现得顺从和感激。 
 B)  表达希望被咨询或告知的强烈愿望。 
 C)  避免说任何听起来负面的话。 
 D)  记下所有医生和护士的名字。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Note down the names of all the doctors and nurses. 
 【定位】 P5 Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse. When people know you have their names, they behave better. 
 一定要带一个能为你说话的人，也就是任何别的人，陪你去医院，并且把每一个问题和答案、每一位医生和护士的名字都写下来。当别人知道你掌握着他们的名字时，他们就会表现得更好。 

 【信号】 建议句信号 Always / write down 。建议落在祈使句信号词上：Always bring an advocate 和 write down ... the name of every doctor and nurse。Always 开头的祈使句、write down 都是典型的建议语气，是答案句的标志。 

 【替换】 write down ... the name of every doctor and nurse ↔ Note down the names of all the doctors and nurses. 同义词替换 write down=Note down 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 Appear submissive and grateful to doctors and nurses. 盗用了开篇 Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful and undemanding 的原词。但那是主讲人反讽地复述『医院想要病人怎样』，并非 Brudney 给病人的建议；Brudney 恰恰主张病人要主动（带人、记名字），与顺从感恩相反。  借用原文：Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful and undemanding 

 B) 原词陷阱 Express a strong desire to be consulted or informed. 盗用了 be consulted or informed 原词。但 Brudney 说的是：病人若表现出想被咨询或知情，反而会被当成难缠的人——这是在描述后果，不是建议病人去这么做。  借用原文：if you, as a patient, suggest that you might like to control even part of the situation or be consulted or informed, then you are considered difficult 

 C) 原词陷阱 Refrain from saying anything that sounds negative. 与原文 If you say one negative thing, they get defensive 的 negative 一词呼应，听着像建议别说负面话。但原文只是陈述『说一句负面话他们就会防备』这一现象，Brudney 并没有把『别说负面话』作为建议给出，本题问的建议是记名字。  借用原文：If you say one negative thing, they get defensive
questions.spoken_text: What does Karen Brittany suggest patients do?

questions.prompt: What do American doctors expect their patients to be, according to Karen Brudney?
options: Cooperative.
Appreciative.
Passive.
Responsive.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do American doctors expect their patients to be, according to Karen Brudney? 

 【翻译】 根据Karen Brudney的说法,美国医生期望他们的病人是什么样的? 
 A)  合作的。 
 B)  感激的。 
 C)  被动的。 
 D)  有回应的。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Passive. 
 【定位】 P5 They want you to be totally passive. 
 他们想要你完全被动顺从。 

 【信号】 want 表期望 + totally 强调 。答案句以 They want you to be totally passive 直白给出期望：want 正对题干 expect，totally 加重语气强调这正是医院想要的状态，是明确的答案落点。 

 【替换】 They want you to be totally passive ↔ Passive. 原词直现：passive=Passive 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 Cooperative. 听感上像『听话配合』，与 passive 沾边，易误选。但原文用的是 passive（被动顺从），强调的是『别插手、别要求』，而非主动『配合』；cooperative 是录音没有的词。 
 B) 原词陷阱 Appreciative.（感激的）与开篇 grateful 含义呼应，易让听过 grateful 的人误选。但本题问的是答案句 They want you to be totally passive 给出的特质，是 passive 不是感激；appreciative 并非此句所述。  借用原文：grateful 

 D) 与原文相反 Responsive.（主动回应的）正是 Passive 的反义。原文明说医院要病人 totally passive（完全被动），responsive 取了相反方向；它恰恰是病人想被知情、被咨询那种主动姿态，而那会被医院当成难缠。  借用原文：They want you to be totally passive

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about a team with vitality?
options: Its members work together despite risks of failure.
It prioritizes recruiting young energetic members.
Its members stay in touch even after it breaks up.
It grows more and more mature professionally.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about a team with vitality? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于一个有活力的团队说了什么? 
 A)  其成员尽管面临失败风险仍共同协作。 
 B)  它优先招募年轻有活力的成员。 
 C)  其成员即使在团队解散后也保持联系。 
 D)  它在专业上变得越来越成熟。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Its members stay in touch even after it breaks up. 
 【定位】 P1 Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up. 
 当人们与团队同伴结成的纽带强到即使团队解散后仍保持联系时，活力（vitality）便由此产生。 

 【信号】 下定义句 "Vitality comes about when…" 。录音用 Vitality comes about when 给"活力"正式下定义，紧跟其后的 they stay connected even after the team breaks up 就是这一概念的核心内容，定义句即答案句。 

 【替换】 they stay connected even after the team breaks up ↔ Its members stay in touch even after it breaks up stay connected = stay in touch 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 的 risks of failure 借用了第 4 段 safe to take risks with each other 里的 risks 一词，但那是讲"优质关系"、不是 vitality 的定义，听到 risk 就选会偏题。  借用原文：safe to take risks with each other 

 B) 未提及 B 说团队 prioritizes recruiting young energetic members（优先招募有活力的年轻成员），录音通篇没说招募，纯属臆造，多半是被 vitality 的"活力"联想出来的。 
 D) 过度推断 D 称团队 grows more and more mature professionally，录音定义 vitality 时只字未提"专业上越来越成熟"，这是顺着"好团队"想当然推出来的，原文无据。

questions.prompt: What do the researchers find out about members of a team?
options: Their differences are likely to impact productivity.
Their similarity is conducive to future collaboration.
Their connections strengthen with the passage of time.
Their mutual understanding stems from a common goal.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do the researchers find out about members of a team? 

 【翻译】 研究人员关于团队成员发现了什么? 
 A)  他们的差异可能会影响生产力。 
 B)  他们的相似性有利于未来的合作。 
 C)  他们的联系随着时间推移而加强。 
 D)  他们的相互理解源于共同目标。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Their similarity is conducive to future collaboration. 
 【定位】 P3 After ties are established, similarity strengthens them. As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration. 
 在纽带建立之后，相似性会强化这些纽带。结果，人们会以更大的信任和相互理解看待这些相似的人，这促使他们去寻求更多合作的机会。 

 【信号】 因果信号 "As a result…seek…collaboration" 。录音先说 similarity strengthens them，再用因果词 As a result 引出 motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration，"相似→促成合作"这条因果链就是研究结论的落点。 

 【替换】 similarity strengthens them ↔ Their similarity is conducive to strengthens = conducive to 
 seek further opportunities for collaboration ↔ future collaboration seek further…collaboration = future collaboration 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 称 differences are likely to impact productivity，但录音研究结论强调的是相似 similarity strengthens them，A 取了相反的一极（differences），且 productivity 录音根本没提，方向与原文相反。  借用原文：similarity strengthens them 

 C) 偷换概念 C 说 connections strengthen with the passage of time，借了录音 similarity strengthens them 的 strengthen 一词，却把原因偷换成"随时间推移"——录音说让纽带变牢的是相似，不是时间。  借用原文：similarity strengthens them 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 说 mutual understanding stems from a common goal，mutual understanding 确实出自录音 greater trust and mutual understanding，但录音说相互理解来自"相似"、不是来自"共同目标"（common goal 属第 4 段另一因素），强加了错误因果。  借用原文：greater trust and mutual understanding

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the team the speaker is currently working in?
options: It is characterized by diversity.
Its goals are quite inconsistent.
Its members have similar backgrounds.

questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the team the speaker is currently working in? 

 【翻译】 关于说话者目前工作的团队,我们了解到什么? 
 A)  它的特点是多样性。 
 B)  它的目标相当不一致。 
 C)  其成员有相似的背景。 
 D)  它通过一种独特的机制联结在一起。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It is characterized by diversity. 
 【定位】 P5 And yet, the four of us have very little in common and are completely different demographically. 
 然而，我们四个人几乎没有共同点，在人口特征上完全不同。 

 【信号】 转折 "And yet" 后才是真意 。前句说当前团队最 successful and cohesive，紧接 And yet 转折，引出 have very little in common and are completely different demographically——转折之后才是关于这支团队的关键定性。 

 【替换】 have very little in common and are completely different demographically ↔ characterized by diversity "几乎无共同点、完全不同" = diversity 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 说团队 goals are quite inconsistent，借了录音 the inconsistency 一词，但那个 inconsistency 指的是"研究结论与说话者经历不一致"，不是说这支团队的目标不一致，原词被挪错了对象。  借用原文：the inconsistency 

 C) 与原文相反 C 称成员 have similar backgrounds，但录音明说当前团队 have very little in common、完全不同，C 取了相反极性，是被前文研究讲的"相似"带偏。  借用原文：have very little in common 

 D) 未提及 D 说团队 connected by a unique mechanism，录音从未提任何"独特机制"，是凭"这么成功一定有什么特别机制"想象出来的，原文无据。

questions.prompt: What do experts recommend concerning being thrifty?
options: Putting aside twenty percent of one's earnings.
Spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy.
Living off a small proportion of one's income.
Saving as much as one can possibly manage.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do experts recommend concerning being thrifty? 

 【翻译】 关于节俭,专家有什么建议? 
 A)  将收入的百分之二十存起来。 
 B)  预期自己会变富而消费。 
 C)  靠收入的一小部分生活。 
 D)  尽可能多地储蓄。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Putting aside twenty percent of one's earnings. 
 【定位】 P2 "Even with an astronomical level of income," she wrote, "to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%." 
 她写道："即便收入高得惊人，要想真正积累财富，专家也建议把收入的 20% 存起来，靠剩下的 80% 生活。" 

 【信号】 原词 recommend 直接领出建议 。答案句直接出现题干同款词 experts recommend，紧跟其后的 saving 20% of your income 就是被推荐的做法——"建议/推荐"类动词后面那句即答案落点。 

 【替换】 saving 20% of your income ↔ Putting aside twenty percent of one's earnings 同义改写 save=put aside、income=earnings 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 的 Spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy 几乎照搬原文 spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy，但原文是把它当作让人沦为"工资奴隶"的反面行为来批评，不是专家推荐的做法，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy 

 C) 与原文相反 C 说靠 a small proportion of one's income（一小部分收入）过活，而原文是靠 the remaining 80%（大头）生活、只存 20%，C 把"靠大部分生活"偷换成"靠一小部分生活"，与原文相反。  借用原文：living off the remaining 80% 

 D) 偷换概念 D 的 Saving as much as one can possibly manage（尽量多存）听上去合理，但原文给的是精确的"存 20%"，并非"能存多少存多少"，D 用模糊的最大化偷换了专家给出的确切比例。
questions.spoken_text: What do experts recommend concerning being thrifty?

questions.prompt: How does confidence help people to be thrifty?
options: It empowers them to cope with irrational emotions.
It will guarantee the profits from their investments.
It will turn them into successful financial planners.
It enables them to focus on long-term investments.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How does confidence help people to be thrifty? 

 【翻译】 自信如何帮助人们保持节俭? 
 A)  它使他们有能力应对非理性情绪。 
 B)  它将保证他们的投资获利。 
 C)  它将把他们变成成功的理财规划师。 
 D)  它使他们能够专注于长期投资。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It enables them to focus on long-term investments. 
 【定位】 P3 It also takes confidence to invest properly. Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investments alone and focus on a long-term investment plan. 
 正确投资同样需要信心。理财规划师建议，不要凭情绪做投资决策，而应让投资保持不动、专注于一个长期投资计划。 

 【信号】 Instead of 否定情绪、转出正解 。答案句用 Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions 先否定"凭情绪投资"，转折出真正建议的做法——专注长期投资计划；"Instead of A, do B"里 B 才是落点。 

 【替换】 focus on a long-term investment plan ↔ focus on long-term investments 近乎同义、概括复述 
 leave your investments alone ↔ enables them to focus on long-term investments 详述→概括 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说信心"使人应对 irrational emotions"，盗用了原文的 emotions 一词，但原文是说"不要用情绪做决策"（避开情绪），并非"赋予人应对非理性情绪的能力"，把"绕开情绪"偷换成"驾驭情绪"。  借用原文：making investing decisions with your emotions 

 B) 过度推断 B 说信心 guarantee the profits from their investments（保证投资盈利），原文从未承诺"保证收益"，只说专注长期计划，guarantee 是过度拔高的绝对化表述。 
 C) 张冠李戴 C 说信心 turn them into successful financial planners，盗用了原文出现的 financial planners，但原文里 financial planners 是"给出建议的人"，不是说有信心就能"变成"理财规划师，把建议者的身份安到了普通人身上。  借用原文：financial planners advise

questions.prompt: How do millionaires react when they fail in their investment?
options: They count on others to take the responsibility.
They change their investment strategy in time.
They think they themselves are to blame.
They persist rather than get discouraged.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How do millionaires react when they fail in their investment? 

 【翻译】 百万富翁在投资失败时如何应对? 
 A)  他们指望别人承担责任。 
 B)  他们及时改变投资策略。 
 C)  他们认为自己应该受到责备。 
 D)  他们坚持下去而不是气馁。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They think they themselves are to blame. 
 【定位】 P3 Millionaires don't count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don't blame anyone else if they fall short. 
 百万富翁不指望别人让自己变富，达不到目标时也不怪罪任何人。 

 【信号】 两个 don't…anyone else 否定推责 。答案句连用 don't count on anyone else 和 don't blame anyone else 两重否定，把责任牢牢落回自己身上——否定"怪别人"等于肯定"怪自己"，这是答案落点。 

 【替换】 they don't blame anyone else if they fall short ↔ They think they themselves are to blame 否定他人=肯定自身（肯否转换） 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 说他们 count on others to take the responsibility，盗用了原文的 count on anyone else 和 responsibility，但原文明明是"don't count on anyone else"——加了否定。A 把原文的否定句正过来用，与原文相反。  借用原文：don't count on anyone else 

 B) 未提及 B 说他们 change their investment strategy in time（及时改投资策略），原文谈的是"失利时不怪别人/担责"，从没说他们会"改策略"，属凭常识脑补的未提及项。 
 D) 答非所问 D 的 persist rather than get discouraged（坚持不气馁）说的是"态度上是否泄气"，原文这句讲的是"责任归谁"，D 答的是另一个维度，与本题问的"react when they fail"对不上。

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say millionaires are socially indifferent?
options: They do not resist novel lifestyles.
They do not try to keep up with others.
They do not care what they have acquired.
They do not pressure themselves to get rich.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the speaker say millionaires are socially indifferent? 

 【翻译】 为什么说话者说百万富翁在社交上漠不关心? 
 A)  他们不抗拒新颖的生活方式。 
 B)  他们不试图跟上他人。 
 C)  他们不在乎自己获得了什么。 
 D)  他们不给自己施加变富的压力。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They do not try to keep up with others. 
 【定位】 P4 Essentially, they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others or what they have acquired. 
 本质上，他们不会屈服于"去买最新潮的东西、或与他人攀比所拥有之物"的压力。 

 【信号】 Essentially 引出本质解释 。答案句以 Essentially 领出对"社会冷漠"的本质性解释，其中 keep up with others 直接说明缘由——他们不攀比，这是答案落点。 

 【替换】 they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others ↔ They do not try to keep up with others 近乎同词、概括复述 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 说他们 do not resist novel lifestyles（不抗拒新潮生活），原文提到的是 lifestyle creep（消费随收入膨胀），并说他们 resist lifestyle creep——是"抗拒"，A 借 lifestyle 一词却把"抗拒"说成"不抗拒"，与原文相反。  借用原文：They resist lifestyle creep 

 C) 偷换概念 C 说他们 do not care what they have acquired（不在乎自己拥有什么），盗用了原文 what they have acquired，但原文是说他们"不为攀比别人所拥有的而买买买"，并非"不在乎自己的所有物"，把宾语对象偷换了。  借用原文：keep up with others or what they have acquired 

 D) 偷换概念 D 说他们 do not pressure themselves to get rich（不逼自己变富），原文讲的 pressure 是"买最新潮的、与人攀比"的外部压力，不是"逼自己变富"的内部压力，D 把压力的对象配错了。  借用原文：they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing
